title: Redundant Boolean Identity Comparisons
pattern: Comparing a boolean variable directly to `true` or `false` using equality operators.
why_bad: It is logically redundant. Booleans are already truth values; comparing them to boolean constants adds visual noise with zero semantic value.
detection: Expressions comparing a boolean type to `true` or `false` literals.
fix: Remove the comparison and use the boolean variable directly (`if flag` or `if !flag`).
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 17 ("Unusual Control Structures"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 17.
